chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The man divorces his wife while she is menstruating.'
He said: 'Divorce contrary to the Sunnah is void.'
I said: 'So the man pronounces divorce three times in one sitting?'
He said: 'He is to be returned to the Sunnah.'

key_terms.السُّنَّة: Sunnah — the prescribed method established by the Prophet and transmitted through the Imams
key_terms.الطَّلَاق: Divorce (talak) — the formal Islamic dissolution of marriage
key_terms.بَاطِل: Batil — void, legally null, without effect
key_terms.حَائِض: Ha'id — a woman in her monthly menstrual period (hayd)
key_terms.مَقْعَد: Maq'ad — a single sitting, one session

ai.seo_question: Is divorce pronounced during menstruation valid in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Muhammad al-Halabi narrates a dialogue with Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) about two irregular forms of divorce. The Imam rules that divorce pronounced while a wife is menstruating is void (batil) and not in accordance with the Sunnah, which requires the wife to be in a state of ritual purity (tuhr) and not have been sexually approached during that period. Regarding the triple divorce in a single utterance, the Imam declares it should be 'returned to the Sunnah' — meaning it is treated as a single revocable pronouncement.
